title: Budget and Revenue
text:
Do bigger budgets lead to a bigger box office revenue? Figure 1 plots each film’s production budget against its worldwide revenue, both in millions of US dollars.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["budget_musd"], films["revenue_musd"])
plt.xlabel("Budget (million USD)")
plt.ylabel("Revenue (million USD)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Production budget versus worldwide revenue for 104 films (millions of US dollars).

title: Box Office Numbers
text:
This site explores a dataset of 104 films released between 1980 and 2025. For each film it records the budget and worldwide revenue (in millions of US dollars), the runtime, and the public rating. The figures are approximate and not adjusted for inflation.

title: Runtime and Ratings
text:
Are longer films rated higher? Figure 1 plots each film’s runtime in minutes against its public rating.

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")

plt.scatter(films["runtime_min"], films["imdb_rating"])
plt.xlabel("Runtime (minutes)")
plt.ylabel("IMDb rating")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Runtime (minutes) versus public rating for 104 films.





The table below shows the mean rating of the films in each decade.

films["decade"] = films["year"] // 10 * 10
films.groupby("decade")["imdb_rating"].mean().round(2)

title: The Bond Films
text:
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

films = pd.read_csv("films.csv")
bond = films[films["franchise"] == "James Bond"]

The dataset includes the James Bond films released between 1995 and 2021. Figure 1 shows how their worldwide revenue changed over time.

plt.plot(bond["year"], bond["revenue_musd"], marker="o")
plt.xlabel("Year")
plt.ylabel("Revenue (million USD)")
plt.show()







Figure 1: Worldwide revenue of the James Bond films over time (millions of US dollars).
